tier_reason: The arXiv preprint (v1, 2026-09-13) benchmarks DiaLSM against RocksDB v8.3.2 (with Sub-Compaction) and ADOC on stated hardware (2x AMD EPYC 7352). The ICDE 2027 acceptance comes only from the authors: the conference is in May 2027, there is no public accepted-papers list or proceedings yet, and no code is released. That leaves first-party preprint numbers, which is tier C, not B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 8KB FillRandom: up to 2.4x higher throughput and ~50% lower latency than ADOC (a RocksDB-based auto-tuner), not stock RocksDB. 94.3% fewer write stalls: ADOC and RocksDB show up to 17.6x higher stall rates. ~50% lower average/median latency than both RocksDB(16) and ADOC(16) (Fig. 7). ReadRandomWriteRandom: 1.8x vs ADOC. YCSB-E: ~1.7x vs ADOC and RocksDB at the default scan length 128, and 3.3x/5.7x/8.9x at scan lengths 1K/4K/16K; YCSB-C at parity. Sysbench on MariaDB/MyRocks: 2.3x vs ADOC on oltp_insert, up to 9.9x on oltp_write_only, 2.2x vs ADOC on oltp_read_write.
corrections.workload: db_bench FillRandom (128B/1KB/8KB values, 10M entries per I/O thread) and ReadRandomWriteRandom (100M 1KB entries preloaded); YCSB A-F with 1KB values; Sysbench OLTP on MariaDB/MyRocks. DiaLSM is built atop RocksDB v8.3.2. Baselines are RocksDB v8.3.2 with Sub-Compaction, and ADOC. For all systems, write throttling (WST), commit logging and block cache were disabled.
corrections.caveats: Venue is author-reported only. The arXiv comment (v1, 2026-09-13) and the repo README say the paper was accepted to the 43rd IEEE ICDE 2027 (Copenhagen, May 17-21 2027). The date fits ICDE 2027's Round-1 notification (2026-09-10), but there is no public accepted-papers list or proceedings, so peer review cannot be confirmed yet. Tier is held at C; it can go to B once ICDE 2027 lists the paper. The headline 2.4x/1.8x/2.2x/2.3x gains are against ADOC, not stock RocksDB. Against RocksDB the paper shows ~50% lower latency, 94.3% fewer stalls and the YCSB-E range-scan wins. The RocksDB config is non-default: throttling, WAL/commit logging and block cache were all disabled. The paper says the code is 'publicly available' at DISCOS-LAB/DiaLSM, but the repo holds only a README ('will be available soon') and has no license. Compiler/flags are not stated.

notes: The record credited ADOC-relative numbers to RocksDB; claimed_speedup is rewritten with the correct baseline for each number. The ICDE 2027 acceptance is plausible from the notification date but unverifiable today (conference not held, no published list), so the tier goes from B to C. Repo metadata checks out via gh: 1 star, README-only, no license, single commit 2026-09-13.

tier_reason: The peer-reviewed PVLDB 18(12) 2025 paper compares F2 against RocksDB v8.11.4 on a stated CPU (Xeon Silver 4314). The F2/FASTER benchmark is public (cc/benchmark-dir/benchmark_f2.cc), and CMake Release pins -O3 -g on Linux. It is not A because the compiler/version is not stated and the RocksDB (and other baseline) harness is not published.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 2-11.9x better throughput than existing KV stores (abstract). Fig. 10 (YCSB + MixGraph, 16 cores, memory = 10% of dataset) averages: 11.8x RocksDB v8.11.4, 2.1x FASTER, 2x LeanStore, 4.6x SplinterDB, 11.9x KVell. Average request latency vs RocksDB: 1.4x lower read and 3.5x lower write (Table 1).
corrections.caveats: The paper is PVLDB 18(12):4910-4923, 2025 (VLDB 2025, doi:10.14778/3750601.3750615), not VLDB 2023; 2023 is the arXiv v1 date. The 11.8x RocksDB average covers YCSB and MixGraph, not YCSB alone. The latency win is 1.4x on reads and 3.5x on writes, not 3.5x on both. All systems ran with Direct I/O and with WAL/persistence, compression and checksums disabled (non-default). RocksDB was further tuned with 10-bit Bloom filters and the data-block hash index via OptimizeForPointLookup(). Memory was capped at 10% of dataset (3GiB YCSB, 4GiB MixGraph). F2's benchmark code is public (cc/benchmark-dir/benchmark_f2.cc; Release builds with -O3 -g), but the compiler/version is unstated and the RocksDB harness is not in the repo, so the tier stays B.

notes: The numbers are real, but the venue/year was wrong (VLDB 2023 -> PVLDB 18, 2025), the 11.8x scope was mislabeled, and the read latency was overstated (1.4x, not 3.5x). Metadata checks out via gh: MIT, 6,634 stars, not archived or a fork, last commit 2026-08-19.

tier_reason: Upgraded from C: Crossref shows the paper was peer-reviewed and published at IEEE HPCC 2025 (pp. 34-41, doi:10.1109/HPCC67675.2025.00037, same title and authors). It benchmarks BVLSM against RocksDB v9.7.3 and BlobDB on a stated Xeon Gold 5218. It is not A because no code is public and the compiler/flags are unstated.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 64KB random writes: 7.6x throughput vs RocksDB v9.7.3 and 1.9x vs BlobDB with async WAL (R-WA); ~7x vs RocksDB and ~3x vs BlobDB with sync WAL (R-WS); up to 8x vs RocksDB and 2x vs BlobDB with WAL off (R-WO). Sequential writes: S-WS ~4.1x RocksDB / 9.8x BlobDB, S-WA ~1.3x / 2.2x, S-WO up to 1.3x / 2x. YCSB-A (8KB values): insert/update/read latency is 27.2%/28.4%/19.7% of RocksDB's. 100GB sustained random write: 1.5x RocksDB and 2x BlobDB on average.
corrections.workload: db_bench random and sequential writes with 4KB-64KB values under sync, async and disabled WAL (R-WS/R-WA/R-WO, S-WS/S-WA/S-WO); YCSB workload A (16B keys, 8KB values, 500k preloaded records); 100GB sustained random-write stability test. Baselines are RocksDB v9.7.3 and BlobDB. The comparison is WAL-time vs flush-time key-value separation.
corrections.hardware: Intel Xeon Gold 5218 (16C/32T, 2.30GHz), 4x32GB DDR4-2933 (128GB), Samsung 990 EVO NVMe SSD (1TB), Ubuntu 20.04
corrections.caveats: Peer-reviewed: published in the 2025 IEEE International Conference on High Performance Computing and Communications (HPCC 2025, Exeter UK, Aug 13-15 2025), pp. 34-41, doi:10.1109/HPCC67675.2025.00037. This was found via Crossref; the arXiv page has no journal-ref. No public code repository exists (a GitHub search for BVLSM returns only an unrelated spam repo), and compiler/flags are not stated, so it cannot reach tier A. All numbers are the authors' own. The earlier '~7x and 3x over RocksDB' was a misreading: under sync WAL it is ~7x over RocksDB and ~3x over BlobDB.

notes: Tier upgraded C -> B after Crossref showed IEEE HPCC 2025 publication. claimed_speedup is fixed: the '3x' was vs BlobDB, not RocksDB. Per-WAL-mode figures, sequential-write, YCSB-A and sustained-write figures are added. No repo to check metadata against.
